metadata.content: Today of Sky Sports Racing: Two-year-old Trophy up for grabs at Ripon | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Today of Sky Sports Racing: Two-year-old Trophy up for grabs at Ripon Clash Of Hearts & Rogue Jewel feature in Monday's Champion Two Years Old Trophy at Ripon; Simon & Ed Crisford looking for fourth win in race in last seven years with Pure Mint; watch every race live on Sky Sports Racing Saturday 29 August 2026 16:22, UK Image: Bank Holiday Monday racing comes from Ripon, Chepstow & Southwell Ripon’s Champion Two Years Old Trophy is up for grabs on Bank Holiday Monday, plus action from Chepstow and Southwell, all live on Sky Sports Racing. 3.05 Ripon - Clash Of Hearts has leading claims Clash Of Hearts comes here with the form in the bank after bringing up his first win at Pontefract in empathic fashion. He then ran a credible race at Glorious Goodwood in a nursery and most recently was fifth in the Group Three Acomb Stakes at York where he was just over five lengths behind the well-fancied winner, Haffner. Rogue Jewel is two from two for The Rogues Gallery team and brings course and distance form to the race as he bought up his second win here at the track just recently. He looks promising for Ed Bethell. Impressive scorer Pure Mint represents Simon & Ed Crisford under Harry Davies after bolting up here last month. The Crisfords pose a strong record here having taken out three of the last six renewals and they should be respected here with this son of Minzaal. 3.

messages.text: What could trigger driver-market drama after new Verstappen, Norris deals?

metadata.summary: After a summer of speculation, contract extensions for Max Verstappen and Lando Norris suggest the elite seats on the Formula 1 grid are locked in for at least the next couple of years.
metadata.content: F1: Why there could still be drama in the driver market despite Max Verstappen and Lando Norris signing new contracts | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content F1: Why there could still be drama in the driver market despite Max Verstappen and Lando Norris signing new contracts Red Bull's Max Verstappen and McLaren's Lando Norris have both signed contract extensions with their respective teams until 2030; several other drivers at the 'big four' teams are locked into deals; watch the Italian GP at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 from September 4-6 Monday 31 August 2026 07:02, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg discusses Max Verstappen's contract extension with Red Bull, saying it's a 'super important message' for the team. After a summer of speculation, contract extensions for Max Verstappen and Lando Norris suggest the elite seats on the Formula 1 grid are locked in for at least the next couple of years. Four-time world champion Verstappen had been linked with a move to either Mercedes or McLaren but instead signed a Red Bull extension that ties him to the team until 2030. There was little doubt that reigning world champion Norris' long-term future lay with McLaren, but team and driver made that official by announcing a multi-year extension on Saturday. messages.text: 'My body started to collapse' - Djokovic falls at first hurdle in shock US Open exit

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic fell at the first hurdle as his tilt at a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam came to a shocking end to Argentine Mariano Navone in a five-set marathon at the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open: Novak Djokovic loses to Mariano Navone in longest first round match of his career in Grand Slams | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Novak Djokovic loses to Mariano Navone in longest first round match of his career in Grand Slams Novak Djokovic suffers stunning five-set defeat to Mariano Navone in first round at Flushing Meadows; Venus Williams was also beaten by Sofia Kenin; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Monday 31 August 2026 08:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Mariano Navone and Novak Djokovic Novak Djokovic fell at the first hurdle as his tilt at a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam came to a shocking end to Argentine Mariano Navone in a five-set marathon at the US Open. The 39-year-old went down 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 to the world No 49 in a match that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. It was the longest opening match of a Grand Slam in Djokovic's career and the earliest exit at a major since the 2006 Australian Open. messages.text: Donald ends retirement to make dramatic Rams return

metadata.summary: Aaron Donald has officially come out of retirement and will return for the Los Angeles Rams this season.
metadata.content: Aaron Donald: Los Angeles Rams legendary defensive tackle comes out of retirement for 2026 season | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to content Aaron Donald: Los Angeles Rams legendary defensive tackle comes out of retirement for 2026 season Aaron Donald has agreed a one-year deal with the Rams after two and a half years in retirement; the 35-year-old joins a defensive line where he and Myles Garrett hold five of the last nine Defensive Player of the Year awards between them Sunday 30 August 2026 21:53, UK Image: Aaron Donald celebrates the Los Angeles Rams' Super Bowl win in the 2021 season Aaron Donald has officially come out of retirement and will return for the Los Angeles Rams this season. The 35-year-old is coming back after two and a half years away from the game to form a defensive pairing with Myles Garrett that will alarm every offensive line in the NFL. The Rams confirmed Donald's decision on Sunday at the end of weeks of talks and almost two months of workouts at the club's facility, where Donald tested whether his body could stand another season. He has signed a one-year contract, with ESPN reporting the deal is worth at least $20m and built heavily on incentives. messages.text: Britain's Samuel causes huge shock as Boulter wins but Norrie bows out at US Open

metadata.summary: Britain's Toby Samuel won his maiden Grand Slam match after an impressive straight-sets victory while Katie Boulter also won through, but Cameron Norrie lost on the opening day of the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Toby Samuel wins first career Grand Slam match as Cameron Norrie loses on opening day | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Toby Samuel wins first career Grand Slam match as Cameron Norrie loses on opening day Qualifier Toby Samuel got the British singles contingent off to a winning start at the US Open and Katie Boulter soon followed with a win, but Cameron Norrie lost; watch the second day of the US Open from 3.30pm on Monday, live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+ Monday 31 August 2026 01:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player British qualifier Toby Samuel claimed his first Grand Slam main-draw victory with an impressive straight-sets win over Tomas Machac to reach the US Open second round Britain's Toby Samuel won his maiden Grand Slam match after an impressive straight-sets victory while Katie Boulter also won through, but Cameron Norrie lost on the opening day of the US Open. Samuel, who came through three rounds of qualifying, stunned former top 20 player Tomas Machac 6-2 6-3 6-2 in just 90 minutes with a superb display of serving and groundstroke hitting.
